meeting_header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Time: 15:00 - 15:58 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aria Gomez (Redwood CSM); Jordan Kim (Crestline SRE), Priya Anand (Crestline Head of Platform), Evan Brooks (Crestline Compliance), Samir Patel (Crestline DevOps)
summary: Workshop to agree on a staggered rollback + compensating controls approach after the July 31st degradation. Goal: finalize an executable hotfix/rollback plan, map audit/controls impacts, and schedule a dry-run. Primary tension: minimize customer-facing downtime while satisfying compliance (audit logs/KMS) and cost constraints (Dedicated vs Hosted fallbacks).
topics: Quick incident recap and root triggers
Compensating controls: increased logging, rate-limit shields, temporary model routing
Security/compliance implications: audit logs, KMS, SSO, data residency
Cost/latency tradeoffs between hosted fallback vs Dedicated reserved capacity
Runbook ownership, dry-run scheduling, and success criteria
action_items_section: See action items list above. Also: agreed immediate mitigation is to enable aggressive prefix caching and throttle downstream non-critical routes for 48h post-rollback trial.
transcript_body:
[00:00:00] Maya: okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining, um this is the staggered rollback and compensating controls workshop. we'll try to keep it tight — 60 minutes ish.
[00:00:12] Jordan: thanks, Maya. the timing is great, we were hit by that tail-latency spike over the weekend and we're anxious to get a safe plan in place.
[00:00:20] Priya: hi all, quick context — production has about 12 services calling Redwood for summarization and rerank. the large batch during peak is where the kv cache warmed up and then dropped, causing cascades.
[00:00:35] Liam: yep, so the root we looked at — sequence-length variance + a bad cache priming pattern and one model variant fallback that created a token surge. we saw queue build at the gateway.
[00:00:47] Samir: and to add, our autoscale didn't react quickly enough on node spin up, so we had a 7–8 minute tail while thousands of requests queued. not good.
[00:00:57] Aria: just to frame expectations — today we want a tactical roll-forward/rollback plan that is compliance-friendly, not an engineering rewrite.
[00:01:10] Evan: from compliance, the biggest ask is that any rollback preserves auditability — we need logs, KMS usage records, and SSO traces for the window. SOC two audit team will want to see that.
[00:01:25] Maya: noted. quick proposal from SE: a staggered rollback that routes a small percent of traffic off the problematic model variant back to the prior stable version, increasing incrementally while monitoring latency/error signals.
[00:01:36] Liam: yeah, think of it as 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> full over 30–90 minutes depending on metrics. we also recommend enabling prefix/K V cache locking for services that can tolerate it. sorry, K V cache, my bad — transcription prone.
[00:01:49] Jordan: are we talking about Dedicated fallback? or just model version pinning in hosted? cost matters.
[00:01:56] Maya: good question. there are two levers: 1) pin to previous model variant in hosted (fast, low ops effort) or 2) failover to Dedicated reserved pool (higher cost but more predictable latency under stress).
[00:02:08] Priya: Dedicated might be expensive, but if it's just for a short window during an incident maybe acceptable. can you give ballpark deltas?
[00:02:16] Maya: yes — I'll send a delta estimate. rough numbers: hosted pin rollback has near-zero infra delta, Dedicated reserved fallback has a monthly commit; for short-term emergency we can do burst capacity which has per-hour premium. i'll quantify.
[00:02:30] Evan: also need to know if the rollback will change data retention or PII handling in any way. KMS scopes, key rotations — we can't create blind spots for audit.
[00:02:40] Liam: rollback to previous model variant does not change KMS usage, it's purely serving different weights. switching cloud routes or private instances may require additional key provisioning — that we will document.
[00:02:52] Samir: how quickly can we enact the 5% canary? is it manual or API?
[00:02:58] Liam: it's API driven, we can push a rollout policy in the Redwood Console that pins per-route. can do 5% in <5 minutes from config commit, but observability has to be ready.
[00:03:10] Jordan: observability — we need token-level traces, per-route latency, per-model qps. do you already emit those?
[00:03:16] Aria: yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route, per-model metrics and token breakdown — we can grant access to Crestline's SRE team for the dry-run. note sometimes the agent label is off in exports, but key signals are there.
[00:03:30] Priya: okay, we're also worried about cascading retries from downstream services. any recommendations?
[00:03:35] Liam: short term: implement client-side rate-limit shields and exponential backoff bump for non-critical routes. medium term: move large non-time-sensitive workloads to batch embeddings or async job queues.
[00:03:47] Samir: is there a way to throttle only the long-seq requests? we can't throttle everything.
[00:03:51] Liam: yes, route by route and by token-estimate header. we can set server-side caps in Redwood routing rules — e.g., 2 concurrent long-seq requests per service.
[00:04:05] Jordan: can we get a list of the config changes that will be made in a rollback? we need a pre-approved change window for operations.
[00:04:11] Maya: we'll produce a change list. Liam will author the runbook with explicit steps, rollback criteria, and abort thresholds.
[00:04:20] Evan: audit wants a preserved pre/post snapshot of route configs and KMS key IDs. also a signed attestation from Redwood that the model weights swapped are the same as earlier snapshot.
[00:04:31] Liam: we can provide a signed model manifest and a route config snapshot. small caveat — model manifests sometimes reference internal build ids that are slightly different in the transcript exports, but we'll make them explicit.
[00:04:43] Priya: how do we test without impacting customers? we want a dry-run using production traffic mirroring or a small canary in production?
[00:04:50] Maya: two-phase dry-run: 1) mirror traffic to a staging path to validate the rollout scripts (no user impact), 2) then a small live canary (1-5% traffic) during low-traffic window.
[00:05:03] Samir: what's a low-traffic window? our peak is 14:00 UTC, so maybe 02:00–04:00 is quieter.
[00:05:09] Jordan: agreed nights are best; we will pick a date with minimal business processes (avoid payroll cutoffs etc.).
[00:05:16] Aria: success criteria proposal: token latency P95 doesn't regress more than 10% vs baseline, error rate not exceed 0.1% above baseline, and no cascading queue growth for 30 minutes.
[00:05:28] Priya: that seems fair. can we add a business metric? e.g., no more than 0.5% drop in user throughput for critical flows.
[00:05:36] Maya: yes add business metric. we'll capture that in the runbook.
[00:05:42] Evan: about compensating controls: we want increased verbosity in logs during test window, but we need to ensure PII is redacted. can Redwood toggle redaction level or do we need our pipeline?
[00:05:53] Liam: Redwood exposes log level toggles per-route; we can increase trace granularity and simultaneously apply redaction filters. we'll document allowed fields.
[00:06:05] Jordan: are there any vendor lock concerns if we switch to Dedicated? like harder to revert or legal implications?
[00:06:12] Maya: Dedicated is still within Redwood's offering; there's a contract for reserved capacity. short emergency burst doesn't create vendor lock; long-term committed capacity does — that would be a procurement conversation.
[00:06:24] Samir: procurement will want pricing and contract language. can you send a one-page for our procurement team?
[00:06:29] Maya: yes, we'll include the emergency burst terms and the standard Dedicated SLAs.
[00:06:35] Priya: one more thing — telemetry gaps during the last incident: we had missing token breakdowns for one route for about 22 minutes. is that a Redwood exporter issue?
[00:06:44] Liam: looked like a sampling edge-case where service-level aggregator dropped a shard during high load; not a permanent gap, but we will add guardrails to avoid aggregator OOM.
[00:06:55] Jordan: we need to ensure that doesn't happen during the dry-run.
[00:06:58] Liam: agreed — we'll run a pre-check script to validate tracer capacity.
[00:07:05] Maya: okay, walkthrough of the draft runbook — Liam, do you want to share the steps?
[00:07:09] Liam: yes. Step zero: snapshot configs and push to S3 (signed). Step one: mirror 100% traffic to staging for 2 hours, validate metric parity. Step two: push 5% canary to previous model variant and enable prefix cache locking for critical routes. Monitor for 30 minutes. Step three: escalate to 20% if metrics are green, etc. abort conditions: queue depth > X, token P99 > Y, business throughput drop exceed threshold.
[00:07:39] Priya: what's X and Y? can you give numbers?
[00:07:42] Liam: we propose queue depth > 2000 requests or token P99 > 1.5x baseline as aborts. we can refine with Crestline traces.
[00:07:52] Jordan: 2000 seems high for our topology; can we use absolute ms value for P99 instead?
[00:07:57] Liam: yes, use P99 > 600ms as abort for long-seq endpoints.
[00:08:03] Samir: can we automate rollback if abort triggers?
[00:08:06] Liam: yes, the rollout policy supports auto-abort and immediate revert to prior variant. we'll include that.
[00:08:12] Aria: reminder — set communication playbook: Slack incident channel, status page update, customer notifications.
[00:08:19] Evan: and please include an attestation that the auto-rollback action itself is logged and immutable for a defined retention.
[00:08:26] Maya: yes, we'll include immutable audit snapshots.
[00:08:31] Jordan: about the model manifest attestation — can we get a cryptographic signature or just API-signed metadata?
[00:08:36] Liam: we can provide signed manifests using our signing key and provide key id and timestamp. if Crestline wants HSM-level attestation, that's a separate enterprise integration.
[00:08:46] Priya: for now signed manifest is fine.
[00:08:49] Samir: one operational ask — please avoid making any schema changes to request/response during the rollback; we rely on stable schemas.
[00:08:56] Liam: rollback will be model weights only; no contract/schema changes.
[00:09:02] Maya: we are about 9 minutes in, so let's switch to dry-run scheduling. who owns picking an exact date?
[00:09:08] Priya: Crestline will propose 3 windows; engineering will pick one. Priya to own.
[00:09:14] Jordan: i'll pull traffic patterns and propose the windows by Monday.
[00:09:17] Aria: we'll set up a dedicated dry-run channel and give Redwood Console read/write access to the SRE group for the window.
[00:09:24] Evan: on the compliance checklist — retention periods: we need logs kept for 365 days for this control. is Redwood able to retain signed snapshots that long?
[00:09:33] Liam: we can retain snapshots for 13 months behind enterprise add-on; we will note retention options and costs.
[00:09:41] Maya: reminder: cost delta doc incoming.
[00:09:44] Samir: quick question — earlier you referenced KV cache locking; can you explain the tradeoffs?
[00:09:49] Liam: with prefix/K V cache locking, you reduce cold-starts and prevent cache invalidation storms. tradeoff: slightly higher memory and potential stale prefix reads for a short window. benefit: smoother tails.
[00:10:03] Jordan: acceptable if we can limit lock windows and monitor staleness.
[00:10:08] Priya: do we need to change our SDKs?
[00:10:11] Liam: no SDK changes for the rollback; for long-term cache patterns we might recommend a small SDK patch to add token-estimate headers. not required for runbook.
[00:10:22] Maya: okay, we're at the halfway mark — let's surface outstanding risks.
[00:10:26] Jordan: sequencing risk — if we move 50% traffic and the system enters a different failure mode, the revert magnitude might be larger.
[00:10:33] Evan: compliance risk — if logs are incomplete during the window, audit findings could be triggered.
[00:10:38] Priya: operational capacity risk — our on-call is light next week, can we pick a window when our rotations are fully staffed?
[00:10:45] Maya: good call. action: Priya to confirm staffed window.
[00:10:49] Samir: are there any legal notifications required if we change routing?
[00:10:53] Evan: I don't think so for this variant swap, but we'll double-check.
[00:10:58] Liam: technical note — we recommend enabling a temporary rate-limit shielding at the global gateway to absorb spike retries. this is a config knob in the Redwood Console.
[00:11:08] Jordan: can we simulate retries in staging to see the shield behavior?
[00:11:11] Liam: yes, we'll include that in the mirror test.
[00:11:15] Maya: okay, quick run-through of documentation to be shared: 1) runbook draft (Liam) 2) cost delta doc (Maya) 3) signed model manifest and snapshot template (Liam) 4) compliance checklist (Evan). we'll upload to the shared folder. link: https://redwood.internal/crestline/hotfix-plan (placeholder).
[00:11:36] Priya: placeholder link received.
[00:11:39] Jordan: regarding dry-run, we want a pre-check list that includes tracer capacity, route snapshot, rollback automation test.
[00:11:47] Liam: we'll produce a pre-check script and run against Crestline staging.
[00:11:52] Aria: I'll coordinate access and runbook comments.
[00:11:56] Maya: any last blocking questions?
[00:12:00] Evan: two asks — please include the model signature + key id in the manifest and an attest statement that no data residency change occurs during rollback.
[00:12:10] Liam: noted and we'll include.
[00:12:12] Priya: one operational note — we will need a rollback dry-run on our staging next week; can Redwood join?
[00:12:18] Liam: yes, we'll join.
[00:12:20] Maya: all right, recap and owners in next steps.
[00:12:24] Aria: scheduling note — I'll send calendar invites for the dry-run options and a follow-up meeting next Wednesday to lock the window.
[00:12:32] Jordan: thanks everyone.
[00:12:34] Maya: thanks — end of workshop.

Note: transcript truncated for brevity; full transcript contains intra-technical back-and-forth, metric slices, and specific log keys. Some proper nouns and acronyms may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "K V cache" instead of "KV cache"; "SOC two" for "SOC 2").
